overview.text: The Assurance or Touching of Thomas depicts the risen Christ appearing to Thomas and the disciples. The OCA explicitly prefers the Greek sense Touching of Thomas over treating the icon simply as a picture of permanent unbelief.
overview.reason: Necessary concise account of the named copyrighted publication; full-text reproduction permission has not been established. Traditional events and published interpretations remain attributed.

blocks.text: This icon of the confession of Thomas is attributed to Dionysius and his workshop and dated 1500. The catalogue connects it with the Trinity church of the Pavlo-Obnorsky monastery and the State Russian Museum. Christ presents His wounded side among the gathered apostles.

blocks.text: The official account explains that Thomas moves from the earlier refusal to believe without seeing to confession of Christ. It also explains Antipascha as in place of Pascha, not opposition to Pascha, and locates the event on the Sunday following the Resurrection.

blocks.title: John 20:26–29
blocks.text:
And after eight days again his disciples were within, and Thomas with them: then came Jesus, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst, and said, Peace be unto you.

Then saith he to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger, and behold my hands; and reach hither thy hand, and thrust it into my side: and be not faithless, but believing.

And Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.

Jesus saith unto him, Thomas, because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed: blessed are they that have not seen, and yet have believed.
